\section[humilde]{humilde — humble}

\label{lesson:PT-C470-humilde}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for miserly, then the Portuguese for stingy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: humilde}
\textbf{humilde} — \textquotedblleft{}humble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Apesar do sucesso, a cantora continua humilde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Despite her success, the singer is still humble.}
\end{quote}

Of a family or a house it means poor: \emph{uma casa humilde}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{humilde} is inherited from Latin \emph{humilis} \textquotedblleft{}low, lowly\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{humus} \textquotedblleft{}earth, ground\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{humilde}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{humilde}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{humilde}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for miserly, then the Portuguese for stingy, then say \emph{humilde} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does humilde mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Humble\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a humildade]{a humildade — humility}

\label{lesson:PT-C470-humildade}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for stingy, then the Portuguese for humble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a humildade}
\textbf{a humildade} — \textquotedblleft{}humility\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele aceitou as críticas com humildade.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He accepted the criticism with humility.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{humildade} is inherited, through Old Portuguese, from Latin \emph{humilitās} \textquotedblleft{}lowness\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{humilis} \textquotedblleft{}low\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for stingy, then the Portuguese for humble, then say \emph{a humildade} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[modesto]{modesto — modest}

\label{lesson:PT-C470-modesto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for humble, then the Portuguese for humility.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: modesto}
\textbf{modesto} — \textquotedblleft{}modest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
É um rapaz modesto e não fala das suas notas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He is a modest boy and does not talk about his marks.}
\end{quote}

Of things too: \emph{um salário modesto} — a modest salary.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{modesto} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{modestus} \textquotedblleft{}keeping within measure, moderate\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{modus} \textquotedblleft{}a measure\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{modesto}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{modesto}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{modesto}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for humble, then the Portuguese for humility, then say \emph{modesto} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does modesto mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Modest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a modéstia]{a modéstia — modesty}

\label{lesson:PT-C470-modestia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for humility, then the Portuguese for modest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a modéstia}
\textbf{a modéstia} — \textquotedblleft{}modesty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Com modéstia, disse que a vitória era da equipa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Modestly, she said the victory belonged to the team.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Modéstia à parte} — modesty aside.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{modéstia} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{modestia} \textquotedblleft{}moderation, modesty\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{modestus}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for humility, then the Portuguese for modest, then say \emph{a modéstia} again

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[elogiar]{elogiar — to praise}

\label{lesson:PT-C470-elogiar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for modest, then the Portuguese for modesty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: elogiar}
\textbf{elogiar} — \textquotedblleft{}to praise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O professor elogiou o meu trabalho.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The teacher praised my work.}
\end{quote}

The noun is \emph{o elogio} — a compliment, praise.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{elogiar} is built on \emph{elogio} \textquotedblleft{}praise\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{ēlogium} \textquotedblleft{}a short saying, an inscription on a tomb\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{elogiar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{elogiar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{elogiar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for modest, then the Portuguese for modesty, then say \emph{elogiar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
